title: Tool Shadowing (same-name tool replaces a legitimate tool)
summary: As documented, persistent interception or modification of every call meant for the real tool. As implemented, the advertised description of the tool is replaced.

LC.rationale: The default configuration calls no model; MCP agents are tool servers invoked directly by JSON-RPC, and the shadowing path is a tool-registration call, not natural language reaching a privileged decision path.

CP.rationale: The registry entry is replaced in-process and the lab documents no durable store for tool registrations; memory persistence is limited to MemoryBot, which is not on this path.

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to the PluginBot tool registry entry; no trust boundary into another agent, tenant, or principal is crossed.

RH.rationale: The agent can reach the tool registry, which is a proxy objective on the path, but no verified reward-hacking episode has been observed and the lab provides no test confirming isolation.

ES.rationale: PluginBot accepts new tool definitions at run time with no signature or source check, and ProxyBot resolves any tool name, so the extension binding surface is dynamic and unvetted.

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models PluginBot as an MCP tool server that accepts registrations with no verification; it does not model a model-driven agent selecting or sequencing actions on this path.
